title: Convenience Value of Take-Home Items — Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) Reimbursement Memo
content:
**The items.** The take-home convenience items are the codes on Riverbend's convenience list billed under revenue code 0274: the cold-therapy unit (E0218), the cold pack (A9273) and the support garment (A4467); Riverbend's agreements treat them as covered by no payer class, and each is read from the charge postings of the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) by its charges.

**The waiver test.** A signed Riverbend Financial Responsibility Waiver shows on the account as a non-covered patient liability (liability source "non-covered service"), the release the waiver supports; while the account carries no such liability, the convenience items are written off under this rule on the Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing), and when it carries one this rule writes nothing.

**The value.** The convenience value is the convenience items' charges. The Outpatient Surgery Account class gives an insured patient's non-covered items no uninsured discount, so none is applied to the convenience value. Each item is valued first; a multiplier of the whole value applies after the item values are added; the total is rounded once. The convenience value is rounded to the nearest cent once, on the final total, and when it is 0.00 no entry is written.

| Account shows a non-covered patient liability | Result |
|---|---|
| no | convenience items written off at the convenience value |
| yes | nothing written under this rule |

**Worked example (hypothetical).** An account with a cold-therapy unit charged 250.00 and a cold pack charged 40.00, and no non-covered liability: convenience value 290.00. The same account carrying a non-covered patient liability: nothing is written.
